text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a regression in continuous batch admission after yesterday's kernel-selection changes. Two hosts OOM'd under heavy KV cache.
jon: Ugh. Any screenshots or perf traces?
maria: brief profile: KV cache used 24.1GB / 32GB, eviction rate spiked, queued batch tokens ~120k, avg seq_len 512. Logs show kernel route chose 'fast-attn-fused' then fallback to generic causing memory blips.
alex: Do we have admission policy that accounts for KV headroom? I thought we had kv_headroom_percent.
sara: We do, but it only runs at admission time — continuous batching grows the batch after admission and can exceed headroom.
maria: Proposed quick fix: cap post-admission token accretion with a smoothing window + explicit KV scrub before kernel fallback. Pseudo config:
```json
{"batch_token_soft_cap": 48_000, "kv_headroom_percent": 20, "post_admission_smoothing_ms": 75, "kernel_fallback_policy": "evict_then_cpu_compile"}
```
jon: Can we instead bias kernel selection toward low-mem kernels when KV pressure > 70%? That would avoid heavy eviction.
maria: Yeah, weight kernels by estimated kv_delta (tokens * per_token_kv_bytes) at selection time.
ops-bot: incident-created id=INC-4531 severity=low assigned=eng-runtime
alex: For immediate rollout, suggest smoothing + aggressive cap; follow-up: add kernel weight and a lightweight scrubbing/passive-evict before fallback.
sara: I'll open a small PR with smoothing logic and a feature flag. If tests pass we'll canary tonight. :thumbsup:
jon: Sounds good. Keep me looped — I'll look at the cfg math for per_token_kv_bytes.
maria: thx all. will post perf numbers after canary.
